title: Auto Loans: Tracing a Returned Payment Fee to Its Payment
content:
Deciding whether a returned payment fee on an Auto Loans account was PCB's error starts from the fee and the payment it arose from. This note fixes which fee is examined and what is read from its payment.

## Rule

- **The fee examined** is the returned payment fee with the latest posting date among those on the loan.
- **The payment behind it** is the one this fee names as its related entry.
- **What is read from that payment:** how it was made (in particular whether it was an autopay debit from a PCB checking account), the date it posted, and the PCB account it was drawn on.

These facts come from the loan's activity; the borrower's description of the payment does not replace them.

## Input, judgement, output

| Input | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| the loan's returned payment fees | take the one with the latest posting date | the fee examined |
| that fee's related entry | follow it to the payment it names | the returned payment |
| the returned payment's record | read its method, posting date and paying account | the facts used to test for PCB error |

## Illustration (hypothetical activity)

A loan shows two returned payment fees, posted on 18 February and 19 May. The fee of 19 May is the one examined. It names a payment posted on 15 May, made by autopay and drawn on a checking account ending in 4410; those three facts are what the test for PCB error uses.
